text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT · latency spike observed for tenant 'acme-corp' in prod us-west-2. p95 jumped from ~480ms -> ~1.2s, p99 from ~1.8s -> ~5.6s, streaming stalls count rising. Paging @sre-oncall.

jamie: i’m oncall, taking this. can someone grab initial triage? what’s the customer impact (% of requests, single-tenant?)

bob: acme-corp is single-tenant instance on discrete pool. CS is getting reports: end users seeing long hangs on streaming responses (some timeouts). they say it started ~10m ago after a traffic burst from a scheduled migration on their side.

maya: looking at model metrics — the requests hitting model "gpt-open-7B-q4" show a sharp increase in KV cache miss rate and very high per-request token generation time. streaming chunk send latency shows big tail.

kyle: infra: LB connection queue depth for that tenant’s IPs is elevated. backend worker queue backlog ~200 -> 1200 concurrent streams. seems like many simultaneous streaming sessions from that tenant.

lee: confirmed: ELB 503s are low, but we see stalled TCP write buffers to the serving nodes for acme-corp. looks like a hot-connection pattern causing head-of-line stalls on nodes pinned to that tenant.

jamie: summary so far: single tenant, burst of high concurrency streaming sessions + long prompts -> KV cache churn -> heavy per-token compute -> streaming stalls -> tail p99 spike. priority: mitigate customer impact, keep other customers unaffected, gather data for postmortem.

anya: can we quickly apply per-tenant concurrency limits and route fallback to smaller model variant for that tenant? that should drop per-token latency while preserving availability.

maya: agree. suggested mitigations (fast):
1) apply soft throttle on acme-corp concurrent streams to 200 (current ~1200)
2) route new requests to a lower-latency quantized variant (rdx-mini-2 or equivalent) for that tenant only
3) temporarily disable streaming for that tenant (fall back to non-streamed responses) if stalls continue

kyle: i can push LB rate-limit for tenant IPs (connections/sec) and add a proxy-level concurrent request cap. applying now.

lee: i’ll trigger a quick scale-up of the serving pool for acme-corp by +2 nodes and increase worker threads. doing atomic change via infra playbook.

jamie: do we have commands to do the routing/throttle quickly? paste them here so we can run with approvals.

maya: commands:
```
# throttle concurrency for tenant
redwood tenancy update --tenant acme-corp --concurrency-limit 200
# route to lower-latency variant
redwood route update --tenant acme-corp --model rdx-mini-2 --rollout-immediate true
# disable streaming fallback (if needed)
redwood feature-flag set --tenant acme-corp --flag streaming_enabled false
```

bob: CS wants to notify customer if we throttle — they expect some degraded throughput. recommend we inform them now that we're applying protective throttles to restore responsiveness.

jamie: agreed. @bob, send a short note: "We're seeing a traffic burst from your migration causing sustained high concurrent streams; we're applying temporary throttles and routing to a lower-latency model. This will reduce tail latency; throughput may be limited for a short period. We'll update in 15 min."

bob: sending now.

kyle: LB rate-limit + proxy cap applied. new concurrent streams reported ~260 -> stabilizing.

lee: scaled acme-corp pool +2 nodes, worker threads +25%. CPU on new nodes warming up.

maya: routing change: switched new requests to rdx-mini-2 for that tenant. fallback toggle left on (we keep streaming enabled until we verify stall reduction).

jamie: any immediate metric change? p95/p99?

maya: near-term numbers: p95 dropped from ~1.2s -> ~620ms, p99 from ~5.6s -> ~900ms, streaming stalls metric down ~85%. still some in-flight long requests finishing.

anya: good improvement. leave throttles in place while we investigate root cause.

jamie: next: who owns deep-dive? need to determine why KV cache churned so badly and why this tenant's pattern causes head-of-line stalls. assign to maya + lee.

maya: will investigate prompt corpus and model behavior. preliminary: customer sent many ultra-long context prompts with repeated prefix that prevents effective prefix caching; also many concurrent requests with identical prompts but different session ids -> cache fragmentation.

lee: i'll pull network/proxy traces and check whether connection handling can be made fairer between tenants. also check if we can shard tenant connections across nodes more evenly to avoid pinning.

jamie: i'll keep incident open, final mitigation: throttles + routing + scale-up. we will do a customer postmortem and recommend they smooth migration traffic.

bob: CS got confirmation from acme-corp: they ran a scripted job generating ~1.3k simultaneous sessions with very long prompts. they’ll alter their rollout. thanks.

maya: recording a few artifacts for postmortem: sample problematic prompts, KV cache logs, per-request timeline for slow tokens.

kyle: noted an edge: some proxy timeout config kept connections in CLOSE_WAIT longer than expected when streaming stalls occurred; should patch next week. creating ticket ENG-INC-5421.

jamie: thanks all — moving to monitoring mode. next update in 15m or sooner if regression. follow-ups:
- postmortem owned by maya (root cause + remediation)
- infra changes (proxy fix, better tenant sharding) owned by lee
- customer comms and SLA note owned by bob

incident-bot: Incident severity: SEV3 -> mitigated (active mitigation applied).

jamie: closing this thread for now; keeping the tickets open. great response. :thumbsup:
